memory_update.text: Utilities with service territories in Northern Virginia, AEP regions, Louisiana/Arkansas/Mississippi, and Georgia/Southeast should remain priority mappings for the large_load_power_demand node.
Firm-power IPPs with nuclear/gas assets and hyperscaler PPAs are highly relevant: CEG, TLN and VST are the clearest current US-listed examples.

The node should be tracked as a localized deliverable-power bottleneck: evidence points to power blocks, interconnection, transmission, substations, and tariffs rather than only national generation capacity.
Electrical/grid infrastructure suppliers PWR, GEV, ETN and VRT map to the enabling layer that converts load commitments into energized capacity.
Data-center REIT/operators DLR and EQIX are not just demand proxies; their relative advantage may depend on powered land, utility commitments, and ability to solve on-site/off-site power procurement.

Need additional Layer 1B passes for private or non-US-listed operators and suppliers: QTS, CyrusOne, CoreWeave, Crusoe, Switch, Schneider Electric, Siemens Energy, Legrand, Hitachi Energy, Mitsubishi Power, Caterpillar, Cummins, and major transformer vendors.
Need FERC/PJM/ERCOT/MISO tariff-level evidence for large-load interconnection rules, deposits, minimum terms, exit fees, cost allocation and queue treatment before ranking candidates.

node: AI data centers, hyperscale cloud, industrial electrification, and large-load customers
summary: Expanded universe for the large-load power-demand node. The strongest public-market mappings are: regulated utilities in data-center-heavy service territories; independent power producers with firm nuclear/gas capacity contracted to hyperscalers; electrical/grid equipment and construction providers; and data-center REIT/operators whose value is increasingly gated by secured power, land, and interconnection. This is research support only, not a buy/sell list.
